html:
Three air force regiments of the Soviet Union, staffed almost entirely by women, formed in late 1941 and 1942 during World War II. They were the 586th (fighters), the 587th (bombers) and the 588th (night bombers).

The aviator marina-raskova pressed Stalin to allow them after the German invasion, and she trained the women at Engels. She died in a crash in January 1943.

The 588th, led by Yevdokia Bershanskaya, flew slow wooden Po-2 biplanes at night, cutting the engines to glide in over German lines. German soldiers called the pilots "night witches". The regiment flew more than 23,000 sorties by the war's end.

The 586th included the fighter pilot lydia-litvyak, who scored a number of kills before she was shot down in 1943. The 587th flew Pe-2 dive bombers and was later renamed a Guards regiment.

The units were among the few in which women flew in combat in that war.
